would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The sole result report describes only a late link-fixing pass and affirmatively states the change is "navigation and verification evidence only", when the PR it accompanies moves seven documents, adds docs/INDEX.md and two convention READMEs, and relabels ten Status headers.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order's Definition of done requires a result report per WORKER.md, and that report is the durable record a reviewer or the next operator reads to learn what happened to docs/. Its "What shipped" names only cross-reference fixes and two removed dead links; nothing in it discloses that omegahive_spec_1_1, port_spec and stage2_verdict moved to docs/reference/, that hive_user_migration, omegaclaw_binding and stage2_spec moved to docs/archive/, that remote_access_spec moved to docs/deployments/, or that the INDEX and the archive/reference READMEs were created. The Reflection then makes the mismatch an affirmative false claim — "This correction changes navigation and verification evidence only; the triage verdicts remain unchanged" — where the diff is precisely the application of the triage verdicts. It also narrates "The first pass" as prior work, but no earlier report exists in the deliverable, so no record of the actual triage exists anywhere. A reviewer approving on the strength of this report would be approving a documentation reorganisation they were never told about, and readmes-restructure — which the order tells to reconcile pointers with whichever lands second — has no written record of which files moved where.
